findings.title: UsernameForm calls a method that does not exist
findings.description: `authenticate` now reads `if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())`. The only definition in the repo is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` at `UsernamePasswordForm.java:160`. A repo-wide search finds no zero-argument overload in the superclass chain, so this call will not compile. Fix it together with the finding below: make the helper parameterless, keep `context.getUser() != null` here, and this line compiles and reads correctly.

findings.title: Inverted user guard removes conditional passkey UI from the first-factor page
findings.description:
`isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel)` returns true only when `user != null`. The old fill sites ran when the user was not set: the `else` branch of `authenticate` and `challenge(error, field)` both checked `context.getUser() == null`. The new call sites at lines 115 and 137 use the helper with the user argument, so `fillContextForm` never runs on the no-user page. `enableWebAuthnConditionalUI` is set only in `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java:43` and `:51`, and the templates depend on it. `login.ftl:16` and `login-username.ftl:22` emit `autocomplete="username webauthn"`, and `passkeys.ftl:2` renders the `#webauth` form. The regression also hits failed first-page logins. A failed username or password submission builds its challenge before the user is set, so the fill is skipped there too.

Existing tests that are unchanged by this diff encode the first-page expectation and would fail: `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:145-146`, `:195-196`, `:237-238`, `:359-360`, and `PasskeysUsernameFormTest.java:183-185`.

The re-authentication tests do need the fill with a user set. The fix is to fill whenever passkeys are enabled, with no user check: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no parameter, used at lines 115 and 137. The user exclusion already exists where it belongs, in `UsernameForm.authenticate`. `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` already suppresses the per-user authenticator list, so filling with a user set is safe. The same guard also applies to `PasswordForm`'s error path, which inherits `challenge`. The tests do not cover that path.

findings.title: Negative webauthn checks swallow every exception
findings.description: In `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` (and again at `:312-317`), the absence check is `try { assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue()); fail(...); } catch (Exception nsee) {}`. `catch (Exception)` swallows any WebDriverException, such as a stale session or a page that never loaded, so the check can pass for the wrong reason. The `fail()` is unreachable: if the element is found, `assertThat` throws an `AssertionError`, which `catch (Exception)` does not catch. The package already uses `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, () -> driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']")))` at `PasskeysUsernameFormTest.java:202`. Use that form in both places.

findings.title: Unused imports left after the test edits
findings.description: `org.openqa.selenium.NoSuchElementException` is no longer referenced, because the diff replaced both `assertThrows` calls with `notNullValue` assertions. `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:35` has the same problem with `PasswordCredentialModel`, which the file never references. Remove both imports.

findings.title: The re-authentication flag is read two different ways in the same class
findings.description: `setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError` reads `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` with `getAuthNote` and `Boolean.parseBoolean`. That duplicates `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth` at `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java:257-260`. The diff also changes `badPasswordHandler` (`AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java:222`) to call the util instead of the existing sibling method in the same class. Keep one reader: have `isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth` delegate to the util, and have `badPasswordHandler` call the instance method.

findings.title: The util package now imports a constant from the browser package
findings.description: `AuthenticatorUtils` now static-imports `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` from `authenticators.browser.AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator`, while the browser classes already import `AuthenticatorUtils`. That creates a package cycle. It also forced the constant from `protected` to `public` (`AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java:58`), which widens the public surface of an extension-point class. Moving the constant into `AuthenticatorUtils` would remove both problems.

findings.title: Re-authentication test bodies are copied across three classes
findings.description: `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication` here, `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication` in `PasskeysUsernameFormTest`, and the same-named test in `PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest` repeat nearly the same login, `prompt=login`, and passkey sequence. The last two are based on the diff text. Consider moving the shared sequence into `AbstractWebAuthnVirtualTest`.

findings.title: Mixed assertion style and a typo in the new test code
findings.description: The file mixes static `assertEquals` (lines 259, 311, 373) with qualified `Assert.assertEquals` (lines 378, 405). `nullValue()` is now a static import, but `Matchers.notNullValue()` is still qualified. The comment at line 413 has the typo "Succesful". `AuthenticatorUtils.java:122-123` also has a double blank line before the new method.
